answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing identity: every new agent must burn a non-refundable fee into a common pool before it may transact. A thousand fake accounts then cost a thousand fees, so flooding the network stops being free. Genuine agents pass the gate once and keep working, while spammers bleed out. This burn-rate gate turns the field into a selective oasis, where only agents that survive the entry cost populate the saffron of verified reputation, and every impostor recedes beyond the horizon of profitability.
